title: Production API Outage Due to Database Connection Pool Exhaustion
description: The production API experienced intermittent 500 Internal Server Error responses for approximately 25 minutes. The issue was caused by the database connection pool reaching its maximum limit, preventing new API requests from acquiring database connections. Monitoring showed a sudden increase in active database connections following a recent deployment. The team resolved the incident by restarting the affected service, increasing the connection pool limit, and rolling back the recent database-related change. A post-incident review identified inefficient database connection handling in one of the newly deployed API endpoints.

title: Production API Outage Due to Database Connection Pool Exhaustion
description: The production API experienced intermittent 500 Internal Server Error responses for approximately 25 minutes. Monitoring showed that the database connection pool had reached its maximum limit, preventing new API requests from acquiring database connections. The issue started shortly after a recent deployment that introduced inefficient database connection handling in a newly added API endpoint. The affected service was restarted and the recent database-related change was rolled back, restoring normal API availability.

title: Suspicious Login Activity Detected on Employee Account
description: Multiple failed login attempts were detected on an employee account from an unfamiliar IP address, followed by a successful login from the same location. The activity occurred outside the employee's normal working hours. The security team temporarily disabled the account, reset the user's credentials, revoked active sessions, and reviewed authentication logs for additional suspicious activity. No unauthorized data access was identified during the investigation.

title: Credential stuffing against VPN portal
description: Thousands of failed VPN logins from rotating residential IPs over 40 minutes; 2 accounts logged in successfully. Neither account had MFA.
analyst_actions: Blocked offending ASN ranges at WAF, forced password reset and session revocation for the 2 accounts, enforced MFA on the VPN group.
analyst_feedback: Check for MFA gaps FIRST. Successful login after mass failures means the account is compromised until proven otherwise. Rate-limit per username, not just per IP.

title: Phishing email with fake Microsoft 365 login page
description: 12 employees received an email with a link to a credential-harvesting page. 3 clicked, 1 entered credentials.
analyst_actions: Purged the email from all mailboxes, blocked the domain at proxy, reset the affected user's password, reviewed inbox rules for forwarding.
analyst_feedback: Always check for malicious inbox forwarding rules after a credential phish. Search mail logs for other recipients before closing.

title: Ransomware note found on file server
description: Files on FS-02 renamed with .locked extension and ransom note dropped in every share. EDR alert fired on unsigned binary launched from a user's Downloads folder.
analyst_actions: Isolated host via EDR, disabled the user's account, restored shares from previous night's snapshot, hunted for the same hash across the fleet.
analyst_feedback: Isolate first, investigate second. Snapshots saved us - verify backup integrity weekly. Check lateral movement via SMB before restoring.

title: Privilege escalation on Linux build server
description: Auditd showed a CI service account running sudo to edit /etc/sudoers and add itself to the wheel group.
analyst_actions: Rotated CI secrets, reverted sudoers from config management, rebuilt the runner from a clean image, audited pipeline definitions for injected steps.
analyst_feedback: Root cause was a malicious pull request modifying the pipeline. Add branch protections and require review for CI config changes.

title: Suspicious impossible-travel login for finance user
description: Finance manager logged in from Hyderabad and from Frankfurt 6 minutes apart. Second session accessed the payments export.
analyst_actions: Revoked all sessions, reset credentials, confirmed with user that Frankfurt login was not theirs, reviewed the payments export access logs.
analyst_feedback: Impossible travel plus access to sensitive exports = treat as account takeover, not a VPN false positive. Ask the user directly out-of-band.

title: Public S3 bucket exposing internal reports
description: A cloud posture scan flagged an S3 bucket with public-read ACL containing internal quarterly reports. No access from unknown IPs seen yet.
analyst_actions: Removed public ACL, enabled account-level Block Public Access, reviewed CloudTrail and access logs for external reads.
analyst_feedback: Enable Block Public Access org-wide. Always check access logs to determine whether the exposure was actually exploited.

title: Unauthorized Access Attempt
description: An unauthorized user attempted to access the organization's internal system using invalid login credentials multiple times. The incident was detected by the security monitoring system, and the account was temporarily locked to prevent further unauthorized access.
analyst_actions: Reviewed the login attempt logs and identified multiple failed login attempts from the same IP address. Verified that the activity was unauthorized, blocked the suspicious IP address, and temporarily locked the affected user account. Reset the user's password and monitored the account for further suspicious activity.
analyst_feedback: The incident was handled successfully. The repeated login attempts were identified and blocked before any unauthorized access occurred. Recommend enabling MFA and continuing to monitor similar login activity.
